steps.text: This is the new drawing package architecture. The idea is deliberately visual: one file for meaning, one file for the canvas, and no hidden layout sidecar in the middle.

The architecture recommendation is to build a new package, packages drawing, in parallel. This is a source of truth inversion, so a clean package is safer than pushing old assumptions through the existing diagram extension.

Here is the new model. Mermaid keeps the semantic graph: nodes, edges, labels, and topology. Excalidraw keeps what users actually see and manipulate: positions, grouping, annotations, styling, and exportable visual state.
This is the Mermaid representation behind that visual. The point is that the source stays readable and semantic. It describes relationships, not pixels.

The bridge is custom data. Every important Excalidraw element carries stable Accordo identity, such as a Mermaid node id, an edge key, and the element kind. Agents can query stable keys without inventing another layout file.
Now look at the actual Excalidraw JSON contract. The rectangle is still a normal Excalidraw element, but its custom data gives Accordo a stable node key and Mermaid identity.
The arrow carries a stable edge key too. This is how comments, agent queries, and merge logic stay attached even if Excalidraw runtime ids change.

The main operation becomes merge, not rebuild. Existing scene elements are indexed by custom data. Matched elements keep human tuned visuals. Only new semantic elements need seeded placement from mermaid to Excalidraw.

A lot of complexity disappears. No canonical layout sidecar. No normal full scene regeneration. No fake host side model of Excalidraw. The remaining hard problem is narrower: merge correctness and metadata discipline.
The package should split cleanly. Core contains pure contracts, merge, query, and patch logic. Host owns VS Code and MCP tools. The webview owns Excalidraw runtime behavior, comments, and export.
The first tool surface stays small: create, merge, query, patch, and render. These tools work on the real Excalidraw scene instead of a projection of the scene.

Migration should be pragmatic. Stop writing new layout files in new flows, convert old pairs best effort, keep the legacy diagram package as an open and convert path, then move agents and docs to the new drawing tools.

The risks are real, but they are concrete. Excalidraw schema drift, duplicate labels, edge ordinals, and comments on removed semantics can all be tested with validators, golden fixtures, and explicit merge summaries.

The first milestone should prove the model, not polish the interface. Lock the custom data contract, scene query, merge fixtures, and one create query patch loop. If those hold, the package can grow safely.
